title: flatten SDK credential surface and variadic stream helpers
author: Maya Chen
description: Motivation: Reduce cross-language friction when wiring credentials into streaming flows and make small ergonomic wins for consumers that iterate over incremental chunks. This PR flattens the credential input shapes across Python/TypeScript/Go SDKs, introduces a small set of variadic stream helper primitives (chunked_iter/streamBatch/StreamChunks) to simplify common chunking and backpressure patterns, and harmonizes retry defaults for auth-adjacent transient failures. Design summary: 1) Credential shape flattened: replace the nested {credentials: {token: ..., source: ...}} envelope with top-level fields (api_key, token_provider_hint, refresh_scope) in all SDK constructors and callsites for streaming helpers. The change is implemented as a thin compatibility shim that prefers the new flat fields while accepting the old envelope for one release cycle. 2) Variadic stream helpers: added chunked_iter(chunk_size, max_pending) in Python, streamBatch(batchSize, maxInflight) in TypeScript, and StreamChunks(ctx, size) in Go. These helpers encapsulate simple buffering + backpressure hints and return the same typed streaming envelope across languages to make cross-language examples consistent. 3) Retry parity: tuned the auth retry policy to be latency-aware (short default hedging window for streams, tighter backoff for one-off requests) and aligned telemetry tags across SDKS so server-side routing and canarying can be coordinated. Compatibility & migration: existing callsites will continue to work because constructors accept the legacy envelope; a deprecation warning is emitted at runtime. Consumers are encouraged to migrate to the flat parameters to remove ambiguity when composing credential providers. To migrate: - Python: replace Client(credentials=...) with Client(api_key=..., token_provider_hint=...) - TypeScript: new ApiClient({ apiKey, tokenHint }) - Go: NewClient(ctx, ClientOptions{APIKey: "...", TokenHint: "..."}). API snippets: Python: client = Client(api_key="${REDWOOD_KEY}") for chunk in chunked_iter(stream, 512): process(chunk) TypeScript: const c = new ApiClient({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_KEY }); for await (const batch of streamBatch(resp, 4)) { /* ... */ } Go: cl, _ := newClient(ctx, ClientOptions{APIKey: key}) for ch := range StreamChunks(ctx, resp, 256) { // handle ch } Rollout plan: staged deploy. Server accepts both old and new shapes. SDKs ship with deprecation warnings for one major release and docs updated with migration examples. Canary: internal telemetry flagged for 72h and two customer tenants opt-in for early rollout. Telemetry: added tag sdk.cred_shape=flat/legacy and stream.helper=variadic to trace spans. Why this is unique: previous PRs converge on retry and stream ergonomics; this one focuses on unifying the argument surface shape (flattening) and adding small helpers that deliberately keep the runtime surface minimal while improving parity in examples and docs. Risks & mitigations: risk of accidental key collisions when both envelope and flat args are supplied; mitigated with explicit precedence rules and validation error when both fields populated. Minor compatibility risk covered by runtime warning + one-release shim. CI & canary coverage described below.

review_comments: Luis: Can we keep the compatibility shim opt-in via an env flag for the first 48h? — Author: We decided to emit warnings instead and gate server-side acceptance; opt-in flag adds complexity for customers.

release_notes: SDKs: flattened credential constructor args for Python/TypeScript/Go; added lightweight variadic stream helpers (chunked_iter/streamBatch/StreamChunks) to simplify buffering/backpressure; harmonized auth retry defaults. Backwards-compatible shim included; deprecation warnings emitted. Version bumps: py 1.11.0, ts 2.7.0, go v1.8.1.
migration_notes: One-line: pass api_key/token_provider_hint directly to the SDK constructors instead of the nested credentials envelope. Example replacements provided in docs/sdk-migration/flatten-credentials.md. The legacy envelope remains accepted for one release with runtime warnings; remove legacy usage by next minor release.
testing_notes: Local unit + integration streaming tests added for all languages. e2e canary executed against two customer tenants with telemetry gated for 72 hours. Load profile simulated 5k RPS for batching semantics; no regression observed in tail latency. Observability added to track sdk.cred_shape adoption.
